key_insight: Autoregressive quantum circuit synthesis works well when errors can be corrected after decoding, but it fails on exact Clifford+T generation as circuit length grows because small early mistakes cascade into large functional drift.
engineering_relevance: For fault-tolerant quantum compilers, the result shows that minimizing T gates is not enough; exact equivalence and robustness to decoding drift are critical for practical synthesis pipelines.
method: Used a 44.8M-parameter encoder-decoder transformer with structured circuit tokenization.
Evaluated parameterized circuits with hybrid post-processing and discrete Clifford+T circuits without post-processing.
Tested inference-time candidate selection and data scaling as mitigation strategies.
evidence_signal: The model achieved median fidelity 1.000 on 3-6 qubit parameterized circuits, but exact equivalence on Clifford+T circuits fell from 88% at <=9 gates to near zero beyond 26 gates, improving only to 22.5% with candidate search and 39.5% with 2.5x more training data.
watch_item: Performance remains strongly length-dependent, so longer discrete circuits may still be unreliable even when short-circuit accuracy looks strong.
paper_title: When Close Enough Is Not Enough: Autoregressive Drift in Quantum Circuit Synthesis
